rationale: PINS that a declaration inside a function body owns nothing, while a class member still owns its class. Found by the lane's new independent `contains` oracle, which is the first cross-check the TypeScript containment surface has ever had: `deriveJavaContainsTruth` existed for java and nothing equivalent existed for typescript, so the committed lane evidence was a `manual_audit` of five fixture files. The oracle reported 8 false `contains` edges on 200 files of an external codebase, all of them this shape. Two independent causes, both fixed: an eager scope pop in extractClass/extractInterface/extractEnum that removed a member's scope instead of their own, and `getOwnerInfo()` being asked a question about lexical nesting that a resource stack cannot answer. The stack-based alternative was implemented and MEASURED first, and it stripped real members — `class K { a(){} b(){} }` lost `K->b` — because the stack accumulates across the synchronous member loop; the tree-based rule is what shipped. The positives matter as much as the negatives here: three ordered members are pinned, plus the fact that a type alias and an interface declared in a body still CONTAIN their own members. A fix that suppressed the false edges by suppressing ownership generally would pass a negatives-only fixture and break the graph.

expectSymbols.name: Detail
expectSymbols.note: A type alias declared in a body: ownerless, but it still contains its own members.

expectSymbols.name: Audit
expectSymbols.note: An interface declared in a body: ownerless, but it still contains its own members.

expectSymbols.name: temp
expectSymbols.note: The member of an UNBOUND object literal. Ownerless, and the symbol survives — an unbound literal at module level already behaved this way, and the method-body case used to differ only because it borrowed the class.

expectSymbols.name: inner
expectSymbols.note: A local of a namespace function. The same rule outside a class: `contains Registry->inner` was a false edge.

expectRelationships.note: A type alias in a body still contains its own members — the fix suppresses the false EDGE to the enclosing class, not real containment.

forbidRelationships.note: THE PIN. A function declared in a method body is a local of that method. Pre-fix this edge existed: the graph claimed the class has a member `helper` that belongs to a closure inside `build`.
A type alias declared in a method body is not a class member.
An interface declared in a method body is not a class member.

The member of an unbound object literal is not a class member. This edge was the object-literal half of the same finding, from a different cause: the unbound case fell back to the enclosing scope, which is invisible at module level (no scope to inherit) and wrong everywhere else.
Same rule for a namespace: a function declared inside a namespace function is a local.

expectRelationshipCount.note: Exact count, not >=1: a duplicated containment row is invisible to a presence assertion.
